text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- The law for equal rights between sexes is not good enough, according to the state office for sex equality. Anne Lise Ryel, leader at the office, suggests a new law which will give employees financial compensation if their rights are violated.

- Estonia's largest shipping company, Estonian Shipping, will seek a listing on the Oslo bourse and the stock exchange in Tallinn within two years. Norwegian shipping company Tschudi & Eitzen is the major shareholder in the company while the Estonian state holds 30 percent.

- A merger between Norway's largest insurer Storebrand and commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse will not be the best option for customers, researcher Tor Andreassen at the BI business school says. Andreassen believes that many customers will switch from the merged company and as a result it could lose billions of crowns.

- Industry leaders in Oslo and central parts of Norway are more positive to the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse than industry leaders in rural areas, a new survey shows. Business managers do not think that the merger will lead to reductions in costs and cheaper products. But they do believe that the new finance giant will be competitive in the international environment.

- The ongoing war between Nordic motorcycle gangs has had no negative inpact on sales of motorbikes. Sales of motorcycles rose by 50 percent during the first five months of 1997 compared to the same year-ago period.
